# 

Learn How Pricing Works with Snapchat Ads

Snapchat Ads fit any budget. You’re always in control of how much you spend and can start and stop your ads any time.

and lifetime spend limits.

## 

See in Advance How Far Your Budget Can Take You

![Budget slider interface showing projected reach and swipe ups based on Snapchat Ads pricing settings.](https://images.ctfassets.net/inb32lme5009/7yCsjsVJoSP6tm8BGRXKYW/70806023a90f35729df7f99b05f70c74/cost_budget-loop.gif?fm=webp&q=40&h=400)

When you set up your ad, you can see estimates of reach and results based on how much you want to spend. Then adjust as you see fit. Your ads will be shown to people who are most likely to respond to them.

Want website shoppers? Snapchat’s ad system will look for people in your audience who are most likely to click to visit your website.

[Get Started](https://ads.snapchat.com/getstarted?r=create&lang=en-US)

## 

Get Started With Our Budget Recommendation

![Stylized ad cost graphic showing a budget card and mobile ad preview related to Snapchat Ads pricing.](https://images.ctfassets.net/inb32lme5009/6WWJkdtIqbTuNFiILmWJ6/384b7965ef8bbb69dad8da82884b2147/cost-icon4.png?fm=webp&q=40&h=400)

You can spend as little as $5 a day, but we recommend at least $20-50 per day to help your ad complete the [Exploration Phase](https://businesshelp.snapchat.com/s/article/exploration-phase?language=en_US), which our system uses to learn who in your audience is most likely to take action on your ad. The faster your ad completes the Exploration Phase, the sooner we can optimize its performance.

To help you get started, we’ll give you $75 in free ad credit when you spend $50.

  

[Get Started](https://ads.snapchat.com/getstarted?r=create&lang=en-US)

How much do Snapchat Ads cost?

It’s free to create a [Public Profile](https://forbusiness.snapchat.com/public-profiles). Beyond that, Snapchat advertising cost depends on how much you’re willing to invest to get the results you want.

What is the minimum spend for Snapchat Ads?

The minimum spend per day is $5, although we recommend $20-50 per day. This amount can help your ad quickly complete the [Exploration Phase](https://businesshelp.snapchat.com/s/article/bidding-strategies?language=en_US) — the period when your campaign first launches. During that time (typically 4 days or more, depending on your campaign objective), our system focuses on determining the kind of people in your target audience who are most likely to respond to your ad. Over time, we prioritize the ad(s) that perform the best against your specific objective.

How can I optimize my budget?

*   Make sure the objective and the goal-based bid type you choose align with the results you want to achieve. Learn more about [choosing an ad objective](https://forbusiness.snapchat.com/advertising/objectives) and goal-based bidding.
    
*   Your target audience should align with your customer profile or persona.
    
*   Install the [Snap Pixel](https://forbusiness.snapchat.com/blog/the-snap-pixel-how-it-works-and-how-to-install-it) to drive more sales on your website.
    
*   Advanced tips:
    
    *   Try different [bidding strategies](https://businesshelp.snapchat.com/s/article/bidding-strategies?language=en_US) and experiment with suggested bids.
        
    *   Learn more about the [Snapchat ad auction](https://businesshelp.snapchat.com/s/article/snap-auction-overview?language=en_US) to understand how it serves the right ads to the right people and then determines how much to charge the winning ad.
        
    

Can I promote my business for free on Snapchat?

Yes. Create a free Public Profile to feature your business on Snapchat with your customers. See how your [Public Profile](https://forbusiness.snapchat.com/public-profiles) can help you engage more effectively, build a following, and sell your products and services.

# Snapchat Ads Cost: What Startups Actually Pay in 2026

Snapchat ads start at $5/day with CPMs from $2.50 to $10. Guide to Snapchat ad costs, pricing by format, minimum budgets, and test sizing for startups.

![](/assets/matt-pru-v1.webp)

By [Matt Pru](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mattpru/)September 3, 2026 · 11 min read

**Snapchat ads start at just $5 per day, with CPMs ranging from $2.50 to $10 -- one of the lowest-cost entry points in paid social.** Startups can expect link-click CPCs of $0.84 to $1.02, app-install CPAs of $1.50 to $4.00, and direct-to-consumer e-commerce purchase CPAs around $23.40. At scale, conversion CPMs climb to roughly $27, and premium formats like AR Lenses and Commercials carry five-figure minimums -- so your real cost depends entirely on your format, objective, and audience.

For VC-backed startups building a [paid media strategy](https://www.stackmatix.com/blog/paid-media-strategy-framework), Snapchat sits in an interesting middle ground: cheaper top-of-funnel awareness than Meta, deeper creative formats than TikTok, and a younger, more engaged audience than Reddit. It is not a replacement for a Meta conversion engine, but it is one of the most cost-efficient ways to reach Gen Z consumers at scale -- if you size the test budget correctly and know which formats match your ICP.

* * *

## TL;DR: Snapchat Ads Cost Essentials

*   **Minimum daily budget is $5**, but you need $20 to $50 per day to clear Snapchat's exploration phase and at least $250 per day to reliably exit the learning phase for conversion campaigns.
*   **CPMs average $2.50 to $10** depending on format and objective -- awareness campaigns run as low as $5.84, while conversion-optimized campaigns climb to a $27.10 median.
*   **Cost per click runs $0.84 to $1.02** for standard link-click campaigns, about half of what you pay on Meta for equivalent link clicks.
*   **App-install campaigns average $1.50 to $4.00 per install**, making Snapchat one of the most efficient channels for consumer-app user acquisition.
*   **Premium formats require premium budgets** -- Sponsored Lenses start around $50,000+, and Commercials are non-skippable pre-roll placements with bespoke pricing.

## What Is Snapchat Ads Cost?

Snapchat ads cost is what an advertiser pays to place vertical full-screen ads inside Snapchat's ecosystem -- Stories, Spotlight, Discover, and Chat -- using an auction-based pricing model. Snapchat charges per thousand impressions (CPM) but supports goal-based bidding, which lets you optimize toward a specific action like a swipe-up, app install, or purchase while still paying on an impression basis.

Snapchat offers two budget structures: a daily budget that caps spend per day, and a lifetime budget that sets a total spend cap. Within both, you set a bid -- the maximum you are willing to pay per thousand impressions or per goal event -- and the auction competes for placements based on your bid, creative quality, and audience relevance. The platform recommends a swipe-up bid between $1 and $3, with app-install bids set at your target cost per install.

## How Much Do Snapchat Ads Cost?

Snapchat advertising cost varies significantly by ad format. Below is the format-by-format breakdown based on published benchmark ranges as of mid-2026.

| Ad Format | CPM Range | CPC Range | CPA Range | Typical Minimum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Snap Ads (Single Image/Video) | $2.50 - $10 | $0.84 - $1.02 | $10 - $30 | $5/day |
| Story Ads | $4 - $12 | $1.00 - $1.50 | $15 - $35 | $20/day |
| Collection Ads | $5 - $14 | $1.20 - $1.80 | $18 - $40 | $50/day (recommended) |
| Dynamic Ads | $5 - $13 | $1.10 - $1.70 | $15 - $35 | $50/day (recommended) |
| Commercials | $10 - $30 | $1.50 - $3.00 | $25 - $60 | Custom (non-skippable pre-roll) |
| Sponsored AR Lenses | $15 - $40 | N/A (engagement-based) | Varies | $50,000+ (custom placement) |
| Filters (On-Demand Geofilters) | $5 - $20 | N/A (impression-based) | Varies | $5 - $20/day (local) |

These are benchmark ranges, not fixed prices. Your actual cost shifts based on auction competition, seasonality, targeting specificity, and creative quality. January and February see the lowest CPMs, while October through December carry the highest.

## What Drives Snapchat Ads Cost?

*   **Auction competition.** When multiple advertisers bid on the same audience, CPMs rise. Narrow targeting like 18-to-24 in a single metro draws more competition than broad national targeting.
*   **Audience size.** Smaller, precisely defined audiences cost more because impression supply is limited.
*   **Ad format.** AR Lenses cost more than Story Ads, which cost more than standard Snap Ads. The more interactive the format, the higher the CPM floor.
*   **Creative quality.** High swipe-up rates and strong engagement lower your effective CPM because the auction favors ads users interact with. Repurposed creative costs more because it underperforms.
*   **Campaign objective.** Awareness campaigns average a $5.84 CPM; conversion-optimized campaigns run a $27.10 median. Lower-funnel objectives cost more because inventory is scarcer.
*   **Seasonality.** CPMs peak in Q4 during the holiday ad rush and bottom out in January and February.
*   **Relevance score.** Snapchat assigns an internal quality score based on audience relevance and engagement. Higher scores reduce your cost.

## What Is the Minimum Budget for Snapchat Ads?

The official minimum daily budget is $5, one of the lowest entry barriers in paid social. For a startup, you can launch a first test for $35 a week -- cheap enough to validate whether the platform fits your ICP.

But the $5 floor is not a working budget. Snapchat campaigns go through an exploration phase lasting approximately four days. At $5 per day, your campaign gathers too little data to optimize. To clear the exploration phase, plan for $20 to $50 per day minimum.

To exit the full learning phase -- where the algorithm has enough data to optimize reliably -- you need roughly 50 conversion events within seven days. For most advertisers, that means $250 or more per day. This is the real minimum for a conversion campaign that delivers dependable results.

Premium formats break this scale. Sponsored Lenses start around $50,000 per day for a national placement, and Commercials have custom minimums negotiated directly with Snapchat's sales team. These are brand-play formats, not startup-test formats.

## How Does Snapchat Ads Cost Compare to Other Platforms?

| Platform | Awareness CPM Range | Conversion CPM Range | Link-Click CPC Range | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Snapchat | $2.50 - $10 | $10 - $30 | $0.84 - $1.02 | Gen Z awareness, app installs, AR engagement |
| Meta (Facebook/Instagram) | $6.70 - $14.40 | $12 - $35 | $1.86 - $2.23

## [How much does it cost to advertise on Snapchat?](https://strikesocial.com/blog/snapchat-cost/)

* * *

[blog](https://strikesocial.com/resources/blog/) >

Snapchat offers a few different options for anyone looking to advertise on the platform — reaching out directly to the Snapchat sales team, using the Snapchat ad manager or connecting with a Snapchat certified partner.

Take a look at how the pricing for these Snapchat options works and learn how to create a budget that will allow you to reach your goals with Snapchat advertising.

**Related:** [Everything you need to get started with advertising on Snapchat.](https://strikesocial.com/blog/snapchat-for-business)

* * *

## Bidding, billing and budget — Snapchat’s self-serve tool has you covered

With Snapchat’s **ad manager** tool, the cost of an ad is based on how advertisers structure their campaigns. Snapchat charges per 1,000 impressions (CPM), but offers goal-based bidding.

Goal-based bidding allows the advertiser to set up a maximum price for each time a viewer performs the action the ad is optimized for. The goal options available are swipe ups, app installs and impressions.

Snapchat recommends setting a swipe up bid between $1 and $3, making adjustments as needed according to the ad performance. App install bids are recommended to be set at the cost per install goal, which is the ideal amount the advertiser would pay for an individual user’s installation of the app. As with swipe up bids, the install bid should be optimized based on performance. Advertisers can also set a daily budget for their campaigns.

Once your campaign has been set up, Snapchat will deliver your ads aiming to generate the most of the specified goal at the lowest cost. Due to budget pacing and user-action prediction variance, the observed cost per event may exceed the inputted bid amount.

While Snapchat advertisers do get to decide how much each specified action (goal) means to them, they are still charged by impressions (CPM).

The budget is set at a daily cost and should be optimized for each ad sets’ performance. Snapchat recommends spending more towards ad sets that are performing well and pausing those that aren’t.

If you want some help to manage your campaign, you can reach out to one of [Snapchat’s Certified Partners](https://developers.snapchat.com/ads/partners/). The Certified Partners program allows advertisers to work with companies that have expertise in Snapchat advertising — such as Strike Social — from the initial campaign strategy to creative execution.

The partner sets up the Ad Account with Snapchat, and a monthly invoice is sent based on the media spend for that month.

**Related:** [A look inside the Snapchat Ad Manager](https://strikesocial.com/blog/ad-manager)

* * *

## Purchasing directly from Snapchat

Snapchat also gives advertisers the option to buy ads directly without the use of the ad manager. In this case, Snapchat buys the media for the advertiser and charges a flat rate for CPM. The rate changes for the various ad formats, however.

*   Snap Ads, which is Snapchat’s mobile video ads offering, start at around $3,000 per month in ad spend.
*   Sponsored Lenses vary from day to day:
    *   $450,000 per day if it’s running Sunday-Thursday
    *   $500,000 per day on Friday and Saturday
    *   $700,000 for holidays and special events, such as the Super Bowl
*   Snapchat Discover Ads start at $50,000 daily
*   Sponsored nationwide geofilters are estimated to be about [one-fifth of the cost of Sponsored Lenses](http://wallaroomedia.com/snapchat-advertising-cost/)

Snapchat has made creating Sponsored local geofilters even easier now that users have the ability to create the filter from directly inside the app. The minimum area a geofilter can cover is 20,000 square feet and the largest is 50,000,000 square feet. The exact price depends on the desired location and duration of the geofilter.

Purchasing directly from Snapchat ensures that an ad will run within a specific location of the app, whereas creating a campaign through the ad manager allows ads to be placed anywhere their bid can win, such as between user’s Stories or on the Discover page.

* * *

## Snapping ads and cashing checks

**Snapchat advertising** is the only platform that offers a flat rate cost should you choose to go directly to Snapchat for all of your placements. Working with the ad manager, however, offers more flexibility to your budget the same way Facebook and Google AdWords do. It’s up to the advertiser’s discretion on which route to take.
